title.narrative: Output 4.1. Increased capacity of Member States to create an enabling environment for entrepreneurship and sustainable enterprises

description.narrative:
1- The Cooperative Law Revision was adopted in the National Assembly in May 2023 which has incorporated the ILO comments, in particular the simplifying administrative procedures, which are requirements for the establishment and operations of cooperatives, and ensuring social benefits for workers/members working for cooperatives contribute to serving as an entry point for further promoting formalization and expanding social protection in the cooperative sector (closer compatibility with the international labour standards).
2- The international experiences about simplified mechanisms for business registration focusing on household business were collected and shared with the Agency of Business Registration of the Ministry of Planning and Investment in their reports and during the process of the development of the Decree on Household Business in 2023. 1- ILO shared technical comments on the draft Law. Comments from the ILO focused on analysis and recommendation for (i) simplifying administrative procedures requirements for the establishment and operations of cooperatives and (ii) expanding social protection in the cooperatives. The comments from ILO were reflected in the adopted Cooperative Law in June 2023. ILO provided evidence-based knowledge to support the VCA in amending the law through a rapid assessment of the current social protection practices in cooperatives. The findings of the assessment contributed to advocacy for expanding social protection to cooperative members, and to provide decision-makers with information and evidence for them to make their informed decision. 2- The ILO contributed technically in all the meetings to support MPI and in the development of the Decree on Household Business by sharing international experiences about business registration and household business in other countries to enable business environment for household business.

Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: 1. Decision 1305 QD/Ttg on the new National Programme on Labour Productivity (NPLP) until 2030 was adopted by the Prime Minister on November 8, 2023. 2. A stronger partnership between MOLISA, VCCI, VGCL, MPI and MOST was established as a result of the consultation workshop on new drivers of labour productivity growth in Viet Nam. 3. A conceptual framework for productivity measurement and reporting was endorsed by GSO with the help of a data gap analysis to help enhance a more thorough understanding about the enterprise surveys. 1. The ILO supported the development of the new programme and provided relevant technical feedback to strengthen the content of the programme 2. The data gap analysis generated a more thorough understanding of the development and operation of Viet Nam’s enterprise surveys, core challenges, and ways for improvement of how enterprise and other surveys are currently administered and built some new capacity for our partner General Statistics Office (GSO) through training on new software applications and models. 3. ILO also completed systemic sectoral assessments in wood processing and machinery sectors to identify major constraints and underlying root causes for business underperformance. Sectoral activities were formulated to address the current challenges and introduce improvements in measures that contribute to the overall sectoral business environments in target sectors. 4. Support for sustainable enterprises and decent job creation is the goal of ongoing partnerships with national and sectoral stakeholders and service providers under the mentioned productivity initiative. Technical assistance also includes activities that aim at increasing the potential of enterprises in Viet Nam to respond to changing requirements in the global markets, in particular, on decarbonization, greenhouse gas emission reduction, digitalization, and productivity skills building among workers at companies. 5. ILO provided technical and financial support to organise the TOT on FIT as well as orientation of the FIT replication roadmap in the coming time.

Output 4.4. Increased capacity of Member States and enterprises to develop policies and measures that promote the alignment of business practices with decent work and a human-centred approach to the future of work

description.narrative:
1. The Social Dialogue mechanism for electronics tripartite partners is established and frequently deployed by the VCCI and Business Association to facilitate the resilient recovery of the electronics industry (industrial relations, OSH, contract, gender, etc.). According to the Ministry of Industry and Trade, in 2022, under the post-COVID-19 context, the sector could keep the growth rate. The export value of the electronics sector is US$114.4 billion, 6% higher than in 2021, and accounts for 30% of the total national export value.
2. On 14 July 2023, the Prime Minister issued a Decision 843/QD-TTg, on issuing the national action plan for law and policy improvement to promote responsible business practices in Viet Nam 1. With support from APPLE Inc. (USA ) and in coordination with VCCI, the ILO published the research report on Vietnam’s electronics supply chain: Decent work challenges and opportunities in January 2023. The report tracks the features of the sector and suggests policy implications for Viet Nam with comprehensive inputs from the national constituents and key actors of the supply chain in Viet Nam. 2. With the support of the SSN fund, the ILO and VCCI co-hosted quarterly sectoral consultation meetings with the participation of tripartite partners at both national and provincial levels, the Vietnam Electronics Industry Association (VEIA), brands and enterprises. 6 meetings were organized in the period from November 2021 and April 2023. A wider range of labour issues in the industry was discussed in the meetings, such as labour stability, OSH, wage and benefits, labour skills. The quarterly sectoral consultation meetings are making good progress in building dialogue habits/culture among the sectoral partners. 3. With the support of the SSN fund, the ILO has developed 3 eLearning courses to equip tripartite partners with more in-depth knowledge of sustainable compliance in the electronics industry. They are Gender equality at the workplace, Factory labour compliance self-assessment, and Opportunities and challenges for decent work in electronic industry courses. These courses were developed based on training materials and good practices of other ILO initiatives. 4. ILO provided support for organizing the training on Responsible Supply Chain Due Diligence for key carders of Trade Unions in Viet Nam
